is_anopheles.evidence: The study focuses on Anopheles gambiae s.l. and Anopheles funestus s.s. (page 1, Methods).

reports_target_markers.evidence: The paper reports genotyping for Vgsc L995F (L1014F), Vgsc L995S (L1014S), GSTe2 L119F, and Rdl A296S (page 2, Methods; page 4, Results).

reports_extractable_genotype_data.evidence: Genotype counts and frequencies are provided for An. gambiae (1014F/S) and An. funestus (L119F, A296S) in the text and figures (e.g., page 4: 1014F frequency 87.8% [195/222]; page 6: Figure 5A/B showing genotype distributions).

african_field_population.evidence: Mosquitoes were collected in Ndjili-Brasserie, Kinshasa, Democratic Republic of Congo (page 1, Methods).

is_primary_study.evidence: This is an empirical study characterizing insecticide resistance and Plasmodium infection in field-collected mosquitoes.

sub_country_location.evidence: Collected at Ndjili-Brasserie, a suburb of Kinshasa (4°19′39″S, 15°18′48″E) (page 1, Methods).

temporal_resolution_within_3y.evidence: Mosquitoes were collected in May 2015 (page 1, Methods).

duplicate_risk.evidence: The study describes a specific new collection in Kinshasa in 2015.

supplement.evidence: All necessary data is provided in the main text and figures.

assessment.summary: This study characterizes insecticide resistance and Plasmodium infection in Anopheles gambiae and Anopheles funestus from Kinshasa, DRC, collected in 2015. It reports high frequencies of kdr mutations (L1014F/S) in An. gambiae and GSTe2 L119F in An. funestus, alongside bioassay results showing high resistance to pyrethroids and DDT.
